terms.definition: Intentionally or recklessly causing the victim to apprehend immediate unlawful force. A common law offence charged under s39 Criminal Justice Act 1988.
terms.examiner: No touching is needed. Words or silence can be enough (Ireland, Constanza); "immediate" means imminent (Smith v Chief Superintendent of Woking Police Station).

terms.definition: Intentionally or recklessly applying unlawful force to another person. Charged under s39 Criminal Justice Act 1988.
terms.examiner: The slightest touching counts (Collins v Wilcock), it can be indirect (DPP v K, Haystead) and it can be by a continuing act (Fagan v MPC).

terms.definition: An assault or battery that causes actual bodily harm, under s47 Offences Against the Person Act 1861.
terms.examiner: The mens rea is only that of the assault or battery: no need to intend or foresee the harm (Roberts, Savage). This is the point most scenario answers miss.

terms.definition: Any hurt or injury calculated to interfere with the health or comfort of the victim; it need not be permanent but must be more than trifling.
terms.examiner: Miller (1954) and Chan-Fook. It includes psychiatric injury (Ireland), loss of consciousness (T v DPP) and cutting off hair (DPP v Smith 2006).

terms.definition: A break in the continuity of the whole skin: both the outer and inner layers.
terms.examiner: JCC v Eisenhower: internal bleeding from a ruptured blood vessel was not a wound. A small cut that breaks both layers is.

DPP v Smith (1961); "serious harm" is enough (Saunders). The victim's age and health are taken into account (Bollom). It includes serious psychiatric injury (Burstow) and infection with a serious disease (Dica).

terms.definition: Unlawfully and maliciously wounding or inflicting grievous bodily harm. Maximum sentence five years.
terms.examiner: Mens rea: intention or recklessness as to some harm, not serious harm (Mowatt, Parmenter). Compare the s47 maximum, also five years: a standard evaluation point.

terms.definition: Unlawfully and maliciously wounding or causing grievous bodily harm with intent to do grievous bodily harm, or with intent to resist arrest. Maximum sentence life.
terms.examiner: A specific intent offence: recklessness is not enough (Belfon). Intention can be direct or oblique.
